findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed food handler training to be missing for some members of staff. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff members will receive license. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the required food handlers training within 30 days of hiring. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers to not have any date marking available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure any TCS foods kept longer than 24 hours are properly date marked. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed all the sani buckets (3x) to be dead in the kitchen and server area. Discussed with employee. Ensure all the sani buckets are actively changed out to maintain concentration. Bleach should be 50-200 ppm. Bleach was 0 ppm at each bucket. Change sani buckets throughout working hours. Utilize test strips to check concentration. Employee changed all 3 buckets - 200 ppm. COS.

Observed the bar three compartment sink being used as a 3 compartment sink (wash, rinse, sanitize process). The facility removed the hand sink in the bar previously without contacting SCDPH. The note from the previous Inspector indicated if the 3 compartment sink at the bar is ever used as intended (instead of one basin being used as a hand washing sink; all dish ware brought back into the kitchen to clean), then a hand sink would be required to be installed at the bar again. Since the sink is clearly being used for washing dishes, a hand sink must be installed at the bar. See previous “General Comments” notes on routine inspection forms. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 8/4/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces that are in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Ice machine in the kitchen has visible pink and black mold along the interior baffle lip. Inspector showed the main cook. Ensure staff routinely cleans out the machine. Remove the ice (do not use) and clean the inside of the ice machine.
2. The steam table (hot holding line of the kitchen) has very dirty water in the basins (red in color). Chang out the water in the steam table. Ensure staff routinely changes the steam table water.
3. Oven in kitchen has a significant amount of burnt food debris and black food splash. Ensure staff routinely cleans oven to prevent burnt food debris build-up.
4. The bottom shelving across from the dish machine (top is a prep table surface) has grime and debris - sticky to touch. Clean cooking utensils are being stored here. Clean the grates of these prep tables.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Inspector will follow-up regarding the above areas on 8/4/23.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed several items within the walk-in cooler to have longer than 7-day date mark. Cook followed Inspector to walk-in cooler to assess. Cook stated that the dish washer forgets to take off the stickers and some staff forget to date mark. Cook could tell Inspector when all items were prepped/thawed/cooled. He re-date marked the items for Inspector. Items included beans and sausage. Ensure staff adheres to strict 7-day date marking system, discarding items that exceed 7 days of the date listed. Ensure date stickers are removed as food containers are washed. Discussed with PIC and cook. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed no thermometers in all cold holding units. Purchase many thermometers and keep extra thermometers on hand. Ensure staff knows to replace thermometers in coolers if broken or lost. Discussed with cook and PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Observed the walk-in cooler shelves to have significant rusting and paint chipping away. Discussed with the cook. Shelving either needs re-painted or sealed with clear coat and/or replaced. 

Interior of the salsa reach-in cooler (server station) has rust inside on the walls. Materials should be corrosion resistant. 

Discussed both areas with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The grill line/fryers need pulled away. Significant food splash and debris behind the equipment, as well as on the walls behind the equipment.
2. The dry storage shelving (with garbage cans of chips) has a layer of dust. Shelving needs power washed. 

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC and cook. Ensure staff cleans the above areas as needed to prevent food debris and dust build-up. Clean before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Three ceiling tiles to be porous. The ceiling tiles were directly above the prep line. The remainder of the tiles in the kitchen were smooth. Replace the tiles so they are smooth and easily cleanable, non-porous.
2. The 3 compartment sink need caulked to the wall. It is partially caulked.
3. Multiple areas of the facility have small holes in the wall (beverage area with coffee maker and soda machine in kitchen, hand sink near exit to bar in the kitchen, clean utensil shelving area). All holes should be caulked. Walk around the kitchen and fill holes with caulk.
4. There is a hole above the chest freezer directly across from the dry storage shelving unit (just before the room with multiple freezers). Repair the hole in the wall. Walls should be smooth and easily cleanable.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At this time there is not a CFPM certification available at the facility. Per the PIC, two employees have completed the course and test but have not yet received their results/certification. Inspector discussed options for getting the results/certification from the company in question and instructed them to ensure that copies are retained at the facility moving foreword.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

On arrival, the hand sink as you enter the kitchen from the bar area has a mop wringer stored in it. The wringer was removed prior to conversation with the PIC, but the PIC was notified during the inspection and is aware that the hand sinks must all remain accessible for use at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without a sign indicating which of the three part sinks is intended for hand washing. A conversation took place with the PIC and a sign provided by the inspector to correct. It is suggested that a small sign is created by the facility though so that it can be placed on the edge of the bar for convenience.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

A line of pink slime with black spots is observed developing on the deflector shield of the ice machine. This was discussed with the PIC and the item cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple utensils stored on the line as ready for service are observed with remaining food debris, indicating that they did not get cleaned properly. Cook and PIC were consulted and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The nozzle of the soda dispenser in the bar area is observed with developing black spots in multiple holes as well as around the edge under the cap. PIC was consulted and the item cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

The sani bucket in the kitchen area was observed to bleach out the inspector’s test strips, indicating a concentration to high for safety standards. Cook was consulted and the bucket remade to correct the violation.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. 

1) A container  of rice in the walk in cooler is observed without a lid. 2) A can of chips in the dry storage area is observed without a lid. 3) Pans of taco salad bowls are on top of the shelves next to the ice machine without a lid. 4) A pan of taco shells is on top of the shelves next tot he ice machine without a lid. A conversation took place with the PIC and they have been made aware that all of these items require lids. Lids provided during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

1) A container of cooked rice in the walk in cooler is observed with a spatula with the handle in contact with the rice inside the tray. A discussion took place with the cook and the scoop moved to dish to correct. 2) A plastic quarter pan above the prep coolers has multiple measuring scoops stored in it. The container is soiled and also storing markers, pens and tin foil. A conversation took place with the PIC and cook and the items moved to dish for cleaning. This container, if continuing to be used, should be maintained clean.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple priority and priority foundation items observed on this report. Education conducted on the relevant topics during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Early in the inspection a tomato was observed to be dropped onto the floor and then picked up and placed back into the box it came out of. The tomatoes in this box were being diced for use in facility prep processes. A conversation took place in relation to food protection and the tomatoes in the box washed during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

Containers of raw chicken are observed in the walk in cooler stored over containers of raw beef. A discussion took place in relation to storage orders and a hand out given for supporting information. The containers were rearranged during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

A bucket of cheese sauce in the walk in cooler is observed with two scoops in it. One of the scoops is metal and intended for prep coolers or steam table style service and has a shorter handle than the other. The shorter handle is completely coated in cheese sauce (including where the hands usually rest while being used). A discussion took place with the PIC in which the importance of ensuring that handles remain a hands only section was emphasized. The scoop was removed during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

A knife is observed stored in the gap between the two prep coolers across from the grills. PIC was notified that this is not an easily cleanable surface/ location and should not be where food contact surfaces are stored. Since the last inspection a metal pan is on top of the prep coolers and is intended for the knives used during prep. Use these items as they are intended. The knife in question was removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, no sanitizer bucket is available in the kitchen area. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are aware that sanitizers must be available for use at all times that foods are being handled/prepared. A bucket was provided during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the bar area as well as the sani bucket in the server area are observed with minimal color change on the inspector’s test strips, indicating less than required concentrations of sanitizer to be effective. PIC was consulted and the buckets remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

A knife is observed stored in the gap between the two prep coolers across from the grills. PIC was notified that this is not n easily cleanable surface/ location and should not be where food contact surfaces are stored. The knife was moved to the dish are during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Multiple shelves in the walk in cooler are observed soiled and in need of cleaning. PIC instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation of soilage.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Employee beverages are observed in the walk in cooler stored next to and on top of foods intended for consumers. Items include a half consumed bottle of Sunny D and a half empty carton of XS energy drinks. PIC instructed to have a storage location for personal/ employee beverages and foods that is separated from foods intended for consumers. The items were removed during the inspection to correctly.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education took place with the employee and their hands were re-washed to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 

Sanitizer was not observed being metered into solution in the dish machine. A little investigation revealed a loose seal at the bucket/ tube junction. Once this was remedied the machine worked correctly. Machine was primed and then showed correct sanitizer concentrations after repeated uses.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

1) Two items in the walk in cooler are observed with date marks from 10/6. Items were discarded during the inspection to correct. 2) Portioned beef in the cooler next to the grills is observed with a date of 10/2. Discussion with an employee shows that the items were from 2 days ago and were just labeled wrong. Label was remade to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival, the hand sink directly next to the grill area is observed without paper towels for drying hands. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Chorizo are observed in a bucket of water. Questioning the chef revealed that they were being thawed for use. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to ensure that approved thawing methods are used for TCS foods.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.12: FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (B) In toilet rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G) Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H) Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination. 

Chorizos in the process of being thawed are observed stored under a dump sink in the kitchen. PIC is consulted and the bucket moved to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food shall be protected from contamination. Multiple Ready-To-Eat items in the walk in cooler are observed without coverings. PIC is instructed to maintain covers to ensure no contamination of RTE foods takes place.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation. 1) The microwave next to the steam table is observed with soiled surfaces. Clean often enough to prevent accumulation of soil residues. 2) Cardboard is observed under the microwave next to the steam table and to be heavily soiled with grease/oil as well as food debris. The cardboard either needs o be exchanged a maximum of 4 hours after being soiled or replaced with something smooth and easily clean able or removed.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11  (P) Peas stored in the walk in cooler have mold growing in the container. All foods intended for consumption must be in safe and unadulterated condition. The container was discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Pork is observed thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. The pork was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13  (C) Insect control device is over open containers of chips in the dry storage area. Insect control devises shall be installed so that: 1) they are not over food preparation areas, 2) dead insects or insect parts do not fall onto exposed food, equipment, utensils or single service items. The device will be moved prior to the next routine inspection so as not to posed a threat of contamination to foods in the facility.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text: 5-203.14  (P) Missing or inadequate backflow prevention device at the three part sink. Install an approved backflow device per Illinois Plumbing Code. Inspector will follow up on the January 24th, 2020 for compliance.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) A drink cup was observed in the dish area without a lid/straw. It appears to be mountain dew and an employee drink. Areas designated for employees to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination. The cup was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. At this time, only one of the three CFPMs at the facility have completed an approved allergen training program. CFPMs are instructed to complete an approved training prior to the next routine inspection.  (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Multiple items in the walk in cooler were observed without dates marking the day it shall be used or discarded by. Items include beef, chicken, rice, sliced onions and cheese sauce. Dates were added to the items during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Spoon at the server pick up in the kitchen were observed stored with the eating ends exposed. Store eating utensils so that the eating ends are protected from contamination when handling them.
